notes.summary: Compound Interest is interest calculated on the principal plus the interest already added. SSC CGL tests amount and CI calculations, the CI-SI difference, reverse questions (find the rate or principal), population growth and depreciation, and equal instalments.
keyPoints: Different rates in different years: A = P(1 + R1/100)(1 + R2/100)... ₹10,000 at 10% then 20% → 10000 × 1.1 × 1.2 = ₹13,200.
Each year's CI = previous year's CI × (1 + R/100), so R = (difference of two consecutive years' CI ÷ the earlier year's CI) × 100.
If a sum becomes k times in T years at CI, it becomes k² times in 2T years and k³ times in 3T years. Double in 5 years → 8 times in 15 years.
Depreciation or decrease: value = P(1 − R/100)ⁿ. Rise then fall: P(1 + R1/100)(1 − R2/100).
Half-yearly compounding: use rate R/2 and 2n periods; quarterly: rate R/4 and 4n periods.
Two equal annual instalments x repaying a loan P at R%: P = x/(1 + r) + x/(1 + r)², where r = R/100.
Effective rates worth memorising: 2 years at 5%, 10%, 20% → 10.25%, 21%, 44%; 3 years → 15.7625%, 33.1%, 72.8%.
traps: Applying SI logic to multiples: a sum that doubles in 5 years at CI becomes 8 times in 15 years, not 20 or 35 years.
Averaging different yearly rates: 10% and 20% is not the same as 15% for two years.
Using the 2-year CI − SI formula for a 3-year question.
Treating a 5% rise followed by a 10% fall as a net 5% fall.
In half-yearly or quarterly questions, forgetting to divide the rate and multiply the number of periods.
notes.examTip: Memorise the 2-year and 3-year effective rates for 5%, 10% and 20%; they let you skip the multiplication in most CI questions.

questions.text: A machine worth ₹50,000 depreciates at 10% per annum, compounded yearly. What will be its value after 2 years?
questions.explanation:
Value = P(1 − R/100)ⁿ = 50000 × (0.9)².
= 50000 × 0.81 = ₹40,500.
(₹40,000 comes from wrongly taking 20% off in one go, as in SI.)

questions.text: What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years if the rate of interest is 10% for the first year and 20% for the second year?
The compound interest on a sum for the 2nd year is ₹1320 and for the 3rd year is ₹1452. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation:
The 3rd year's interest = the 2nd year's interest + interest on it for one year.
Interest on ₹1320 for 1 year = 1452 − 1320 = ₹132.
Rate = 132 × 100/1320 = 10% per annum.

questions.text: A sum of money amounts to ₹6050 in 2 years and to ₹6655 in 3 years at compound interest, compounded annually. What is the sum?
questions.explanation:
Interest in the 3rd year = 6655 − 6050 = ₹605, which is interest on ₹6050 for 1 year.
Rate = 605 × 100/6050 = 10%.
P = 6050/(1.1)² = 6050/1.21 = ₹5000.

questions.text: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at compound interest, compounded annually. In how many years will it become 8 times itself?
questions.explanation:
At CI the sum multiplies by 2 every 5 years.
8 = 2³, so it needs 3 such periods.
Time = 3 × 5 = 15 years.
(35 years would be the SI answer; CI does not grow linearly.)

questions.text: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 8% per annum is ₹48. What is the sum?
What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹10,000 for 3 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually?
The population of a town is 1,60,000. It increases by 5% in the first year and decreases by 10% in the second year. What is the population at the end of 2 years?
The compound interest on a sum for 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually, is ₹525. What will be the simple interest on the same sum for double the time at half the rate?
questions.explanation:
CI for 2 years at 10% = 21% of P, so 0.21P = 525 and P = ₹2500.
New time = 4 years and new rate = 5%.
SI = 2500 × 5 × 4/100 = ₹500.

questions.text: A loan of ₹2100 is to be repaid in two equal annual instalments at 10% per annum compound interest. What is the value of each instalment?
questions.explanation:
Let each instalment be ₹x. The present values of the instalments must add up to the loan.
x/1.1 + x/(1.1)² = 2100
x × (1.1 + 1)/1.21 = 2100, so 2.1x = 2541.
x = ₹1210.
Check: after year 1 the debt is 2310 − 1210 = 1100; after year 2 it is 1210 − 1210 = 0.
